body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-09. Full inventory: notes/SPA-ORDINARY-USER-PARITY-AUDIT.md (outer
workspace, gitignored). Companion to notes/SPA-ROOT-CUTOVER-DESIGN.md.

WHY THIS EXISTS: the cutover design note concluded "ordinary user: SPA is ready as the
default; administrator: SPA is not self-sufficient." A Discord report from user Aoife
(2026-07-16) contradicted the first clause — she hit a missing ORDINARY-user control
(per-shelf Kobo sync on smart shelves, since fixed in v4.1.19, see F-c78e8c). The
question was whether that was isolated. It is not.

A surface-by-surface audit of non-admin surfaces found ~30 controls present in classic
with no semantic SPA equivalent. The verdict "ordinary user: SPA is ready as the
default" DOES NOT HOLD as written.

The load-bearing ones, each verified in-tree:

- Kobo account provisioning/repair. Classic user_edit.html:328-337 offers create/view/
  delete Kobo token and force-full-sync. SPA Account.tsx exposes only
  kobo_only_shelves_sync. A user can tune Kobo shelf behaviour but cannot CONNECT or
  REPAIR the integration. (Independently confirmed.)
- "Automatically send new books to my eReader(s)" (user_edit.html:246). ZERO
  occurrences of auto_send anywhere in frontend/src. (Independently confirmed.)
- Advanced search: custom columns (search_form.html has 24 refs), plus exclude-series,
  exclude-languages, include/exclude-shelves. AdvancedSearch.tsx has none. On libraries
  organised by custom columns, existing searches become impossible in the default UI.
  (Independently confirmed.)
- Smart-shelf "Share with Everyone" and "Expose in my OPDS feed"
  (magic_shelf_edit.html:442-462) — absent from the SPA smart-shelf editor. Same class
  and same screen as Aoife's bug.
- Per-shelf OPDS exposure on ordinary shelves (shelf_edit.html:25-30) — the SPA offers
  the account-wide "OPDS only selected shelves" mode while omitting the per-shelf
  selector that makes the mode useful.
- Hardcover token + per-book sync blacklists (user_edit.html:320-326,
  book_edit.html:284-302) — data-routing/privacy controls, not cosmetics.
- OAuth link/unlink (user_edit.html:302-318).
- Add-entire-search-result and add-entire-series to a shelf. BulkBar operates only on
  explicitly selected IDs. `useAddSeriesToShelf` exists at queries.ts:446 with EXACTLY
  ONE occurrence in the tree — the definition. No caller. (Independently confirmed.)
- EPUB manual bookmarks and annotation NOTES (SPA sends CFI/text/colour only; existing
  notes render but cannot be authored or edited).
- Comic reader: direction (RTL), long-strip, fit, rotation — SPA has page navigation only.

RELATED CLASS: F-1a7d85 (SPA hides a control where classic disables-with-explanation).
The audit found that is also systemic, not a one-off — several config/authorization
gates remove an action rather than showing it disabled with a reason.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE CUTOVER: the right invariant is not pixel parity. It is that
every operation a non-admin could perform before the upgrade stays reachable after it —
natively or through a CONTEXTUAL, durable legacy link, not a generic "back to classic"
menu item. The tree does not currently meet that. The audit's §4 carries the must-fix-
before-flip vs can-follow-after split.

CORROBORATION: 17 open "New UI" issues filed by real users (not new-usemame) between
2026-06-30 and 2026-08-03, mostly ordinary-user surfaces. One (#613, @iroQuai) asks us
to mark the new UI as beta. #867 (@auspex) is a user-filed shelf-parity umbrella whose
back-link inconsistency (Shelf.tsx:88,185 "All shelves" vs MagicShelfView.tsx:65,110
"Library") is still live at v4.1.33, reported at v4.1.11.

CAVEAT: source-level audit. PDF-reader parity is explicitly NOT established — the SPA
delegates to an iframe and that needs a real browser/device matrix, not a grep.
title: SPA ordinary-user parity gap is systemic, not isolated — ~30 classic controls have no SPA equivalent
